newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe set for narrow seat win - poll.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe set for narrow seat win - poll.

text.p: Unpopular French Prime Minister Alain Juppe should narrowly win a seat in parliament from his Bordeaux constituency in southwestern France, according to an opinion poll released on Sunday.

The CSA poll for the daily Le Figaro found that Juppe, who is leading the centre-right government's campaign in the May 27-June 1 snap National Assembly election, would win in the second, run-off round with just 52 percent of the vote.
Socialist opponent Gilles Savary would win 48 percent of the run-off vote.
Juppe will face 14 opponents in the first round vote.
His popularity with voters nationally ranks towards the bottom in modern French history.
He has refused to say whether he wants to stay on as prime minister should the centre-right remain in power.
President Jacques Chirac, a fellow Gaullist, has given no hint whether he will reappoint Juppe.
The CSA poll was based on interviews with 605 registered Bordeaux voters and was conducted on Saturday.
